newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton settles higher as specs cover shorts.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton settles higher as specs cover shorts.

text.p: NYCE cotton closed slightly down in rangebound and featureless activity.

Market sources said prices should move higher as speculators believed to be holding heavy net short positions basis the July will have to buy in order to offset those positions prior to the contract's expiry on June 24.
Trade selling should blunt gains however, forcing the market to trade in a mostly sideways pattern before the U.S. Department of Agriculture releases its revised estimate of planted cotton area.
The March estimate put area at 14.48 million acres, but industry sources believe that number has declined.
Tuesday, private analyst Sparks Cos pegged planted area at 13.89 million acres.
Traders also await Thursday's weekly export and sales report.
The new-crop December contract settled at 75.40 cents a lb, down 0.14 cent. Spot July ended 0.13 lower at 72.53 cents, while the rest of the board finished 0.07 higher to 0.15 lower.
As of early Tuesday, open interest in July stood at 17,793 lots, down 1,378 lots from the previous session.
Trade scale-up selling could cap gains around 76.00 cents in the December contract, but floods and rain in the Delta could provide some support for new-crop futures, analysts said.
Volume was estimated at 11,500 lots compared with Tuesday's official 11,618 lots.
